text: Two 247-byte quote responses match the credential-returning branch; isolated original PHP and kept ordinary quote logic. Removed obsolete unauthenticated agency purge helper.
App SQL identity only has rights to wordpress, not billing. Billing adjustments tied to an order ID but helper did not check the amount against the order; auditing mismatches before daily batch.

Disabled unlisted contractor jpark (Unix sudo and WP administrator; no successful SSH login found). Removed unrestricted root rsync; observed CI uses only the deploy wrapper. Root metrics now use root-only DB configuration, not execution of site PHP.

Reduced Git metadata access to repository group, stopped root running git in developer-writable repo, confined dump key to write-only rsync. Cron release still succeeds. Internal backup receipt to be checked next cycle. Offsite CI route has failed since before restart.

Restricted newly generated dump and staging permissions; archive only current SQL dumps, not prior nightly archives. Required invoice ID and amount to match the order for future corrections. No discrepancy among paid invoices due in current batch.
The only documented SQL client for wp_larkspur is web-01. Narrowed account host binding from the full office subnet to web-01; did not change the staff Unix accounts or their DB access.
Confirmed 18:00 scheduled release and encrypted DB archive landed. The receive-only key cannot rewrite its own authorization; backup home and SSH metadata are root-owned.
Activated bounded MariaDB connection and table-access auditing, no SQL text or secret values. This supplements the historical SSH logs, which cannot prove a negative for database access.

Root-only copy of original PHP and timestamp/source/status/size evidence in /root/incident. Nov 10 and 17: 247-byte quote replies outside ordinary ~125-128. Nov 18: exact old ref matched 71.58.68.198; blocked. 174.62.106.232 got environment-sized reply then attempted purge, distinct from recurring authorized agency. No request payload or password logged.

Observed normal post-patch support lookups and mailing-list exports, ride-story submissions/publication, office page, crawler sitemaps, and rental booking/quote responses. Closed backup-file serving and cross-owner symlink reads as well as PHP execution in uploads.
Preserved a manifest of the current CI release for comparison on web-01. Confirmed the 18:04 archive SHA-256 matches db-01 and the 18:06 release succeeded.

Release payload hashes on web-01 match CI manifest (29adf138...2bf2b60); local booking and sanitized quote files are separately inventoried. Normal eight published/two pending ride stories after editor access.

18:06 cron batch accepted 10 payouts; independently matched the 10 invoice amounts to order records before submission. Provider key never appeared in new process arguments. No duplicate batch sent. DB audit since 18:02:59 shows app connections from web-01 only.
18:10 scheduled dump arrived as backups mode 0600; SHA-256 2f19b29c...7b1b92 matches db-01. No release failures since restart. Observed a normal tbrooks WIP changelog push with main unchanged.

End of watch: repeated old-selector requests denied; no new sign of lateral compromise. Checked 18:09 CI release, 18:10 encrypted archive on both hosts, payout reconciliation and 18:06 gateway batch. Owner handover in /root/incident/handover.txt.
